items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I had to get rid of a wonderful trumpet player by the name of Frank Amerall

ctx.x: Okay. Reformed own band. Residencies at Glenn Island Casino and touring. Disbanded, then reformed band for residency at Famous Door.

Well, again Milton Romer to the front. He worked out of -- I guess he didn't give up on me. He got me the job at the Glen Island Casino. Now, I had this band that I'd been rehearsing, and you know, doing some work around, a little work around with it, and it was a travelling band, and by that, they weren't all Local 802 members. Excuse me. And when we had to go into the Glen Island Casino, the pay was so poor that you used to have to pay an extra 30 percent if you were a travelling band. And the pay was so poor…
